# DihLay

### Tempo Synced Delay with Tone Shaping, Ducking and Ping-Pong

A VST3 delay for Windows. The delay time lives on a visual timeline that draws
the repeat pattern you are about to hear, so feedback, pan and bounce are things
you can see rather than guess at. Written in C++20 on JUCE.

![DihLay interface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClyntiaAikaHanaa/DihLay/HEAD/Screenshot/Main.png)

## What it does

A delay is one of the few effects where the control you reach for most is also
the one that is hardest to judge from a number. "375 ms" tells you nothing about
whether the repeats will sit in the pocket, and the moment feedback and ping-pong
are involved you are listening blind.

DihLay puts the delay time on a timeline and draws the repeats underneath it.
Bar height follows the feedback decay, bars sit above the centre line for the
left channel and below for the right, Bounce alternates the sides and Mix drives
the brightness of the whole group. Move a knob and the pattern moves with it.

Three things shape the design:

1. **See the repeats, not just the number.** The echo display is driven by the
   same values the audio thread uses, so it is a readout, not a decoration.
2. **Zero reported latency.** Nothing looks ahead, including the duck detector,
   so it stays usable while tracking and on live inserts.
3. **Safe at the extremes.** The feedback loop is provably bounded. Loop gain can
   never exceed the Feedback setting, at any Tone position. See
   Design notes for why that is not automatic.

## Features

### Engine

- Fractional-delay line with linear interpolation and a 60 ms time ramp, giving
  the tape-style pitch glide when the time is swept instead of a click.
- Tilt tone control inside the feedback path, so the shaping compounds with each
  repeat rather than being applied once.
- Padé `tanh` soft clipper and a DC blocker in the loop: feedback at 100 % pushes
  towards self oscillation and stays bounded.
- Ping-pong routing that injects the mono sum into the left line only and
  cross-feeds the two lines, so repeats genuinely alternate.
- Ducking from a rectified peak follower on the dry signal, with fixed 5 ms
  attack and 220 ms release and no lookahead.
- Constant-power panning applied to the wet signal only; the dry path is never
  touched.

### Tempo sync

- Fifteen note values from 1/32 to a full bar, including triplets and dotted.
- Follows both host BPM **and** time signature, so "1 Bar" is derived from the
  meter rather than assumed to be 4/4.
- The readout shows the resolved millisecond value and the tempo it came from.

### Interface

- Resizable from 75 % to 200 % by dragging the bottom-right grip, with the
  aspect ratio locked. The whole UI is laid out once at a fixed design size and
  scaled by a single transform, so every element tracks the render scale exactly.
- Arc-indicator knobs with the value inside the ring; bipolar controls fill
  outwards from twelve o'clock so "no change" reads as an empty ring.
- Status bar describing whatever is under the pointer.
- Click the readout to type an exact time; typing while synced drops back to
  free running.
- Double-click any control to return it to its default.

## Controls

| Control | Range | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Delay Time** | 1 – 2000 ms, or 1/32 – 1 bar | 200 ms | Time between the dry signal and the first repeat. Drag the timeline, or click the readout to type a value. |
| **Tone** | −100 … +100 | 0 | Tonal character of the repeats, dark to bright. Cut-only tilt at 700 Hz inside the feedback path. |
| **Feedback** | 0 – 100 % | 35 % | How much of the delay returns to the input, setting the number of repeats. |
| **Pan** | −100 … +100 | 0 | Stereo position of the delayed signal, independent of the dry. With Bounce on, the centre point the repeats alternate around. |
| **Duck** | 0 – 100 % | 0 % | Pushes the repeats down while the input is playing, so the delay stays out of the way of the source. |
| **Bounce** | On / Off | Off | Makes each repeat jump between the left and right channels. |
| **Mix** | 0 – 100 % | 30 % | Balance between the dry and the delayed signal. |

## Installation

Grab `DihLay.vst3` from the releases page and drop it in your VST3 folder:

```
C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3
```

Rescan plugins in your DAW. Building from source? `deploy.ps1` does this step
for you.

## Building from source

Requires the Visual Studio Build Tools (MSVC and the Windows SDK). CMake and
Ninja can come from pip if they are not already installed:

```bash
python -m pip install cmake ninja
```

Fetch JUCE next to the sources, since it is not vendored in this repository:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --branch 8.0.10 https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE.git JUCE
```

Then build and install:

```bash
powershell -File build.ps1
```

```bash
powershell -File deploy.ps1
```

Artefacts land in `build/DihLay_artefacts/Release/`. `deploy.ps1` copies the
bundle to the system VST3 folder, falling back to
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Common\VST3` if that needs elevation.

## Verifying a build

The repository ships its own miniature VST3 host rather than relying on a DAW
for smoke testing:

```bash
powershell -File Tools/build_smoketest.ps1
```

It loads the built bundle, connects the component and controller the way a real
host does, and checks that the module exports correctly, every parameter is
published, latency is reported as zero, both mono-in/stereo-out and
stereo-in/stereo-out are accepted, a repeat lands on the configured time in free
and synced modes, Bounce alternates channels, the tail decays to true silence at
both Tone extremes, and nothing produces NaN, Inf or a runaway tail at maximum
feedback.

To look at the interface without a DAW, configure once with
`-DDIHLAY_BUILD_UIPREVIEW=ON` and run `DihLayUIPreview.exe `. It
renders the real editor in a set of parameter states, and at both ends of the
scale range, straight to PNG.

## Design notes

**Tone is cut only, and that is load-bearing.** Turning Tone up attenuates the
lows and leaves the highs at unity rather than boosting the highs. Anything
inside a feedback loop with a gain above 1 makes the loop gain for that band
exceed unity, and the tail then grows on every pass instead of decaying. An
earlier build used a symmetric ±6 dB tilt and did exactly that. At Tone ±100 the
loop gain reached `0.6 × 0.985 × 1.995 = 1.18` at only 60 % feedback, so repeats
piled up and never stopped, held in check by the soft clipper alone. With
cut-only gains the worst-case magnitude of the complementary one-pole split is
exactly 1.0, so loop gain can never exceed the Feedback setting. Current cut
depth is 9 dB, and `Tools/smoketest.cpp` guards this at both extremes.

**Duck has no lookahead.** A lookahead detector would duck the repeats slightly
before the transient that causes them, which is cleaner, but it costs latency the
plugin then has to report. Zero added latency was worth more here.

**The delay buffer is a fixed 4 seconds per instance.** That covers the whole
1–2000 ms free range with smoothing headroom and a 4/4 bar down to 60 BPM, at
roughly 1.5 MB per instance at 48 kHz, so dozens of instances stay cheap. Sync
values longer than the buffer are clamped rather than reallocating on the audio
thread.

**Never transform the editor itself.** JUCE asserts on it, because the host owns
the editor's transform for its own DPI handling. Scaling is applied to a child
panel instead. Related: read the stored scale *before* calling
`setResizeLimits()`, which constrains the still-empty bounds up to the minimum
size and fires `resized()`.

**The logo is code, not an asset.** `dihlay::ui::drawLogo()` in
Source/Widgets.h is the single source of truth; no image file
is baked into the plugin. The UI preview tool exports it to PNG from that same
function, so an exported asset can never drift from what the plugin draws. Those
exports land in `Branding/` and are treated as build output rather than sources,
so they are not tracked.

`Screenshot/make_logo.ps1` composites the transparent mark onto a dark plate for
the README, since cream bars on transparency are invisible on GitHub's light
theme. It reads `Branding/dihlay-mark-512.png`, so regenerate that first:

```bash
DihLayUIPreview.exe Branding
```

## Project layout

```
CMakeLists.txt          build definition
build.ps1               configure and build, x64 Release
deploy.ps1              install into the standard VST3 folder
Source/
  Params.*              parameter IDs, ranges, defaults, status-bar copy
  DihLayDSP.h           delay line, tilt filter, DC blocker, envelope, panning
  PluginProcessor.*     audio engine and host integration
  PluginEditor.*        resizable wrapper, applies the render scale
  MainPanel.*           the interface, laid out at a fixed design size
  DelayTimePanel.*      timeline, echo display, readout, sync controls
  Widgets.h             arc knob, pill toggle, icon buttons, logo mark
  DihLayTheme.h         colours and fonts
  DihLayLookAndFeel.h   themed combo box, popup menu and resize grip
Tools/
  smoketest.cpp         miniature VST3 host that verifies the built bundle
  uipreview.cpp         renders the editor and the logo to PNG
Screenshot/             README images and the logo compositing script
```
